Top risks (brief): 1) Technical — rules/permissions refactor or CRM sync causes evaluation errors, latency or data integrity issues; 2) UX/product — CSM change fatigue or score misclassification that reduces trust and WAU; 3) GTM/adoption — pilot selection or expectation mismatch produces weak signals and prevents credible case studies.  
Technical early warnings & mitigations: alert on rule‑evaluation error rate (>1% of evaluations), latency (>2x baseline), or support incident spike (>3 pilot tickets/week); mitigate with strict canary rollouts, feature flags + one‑click rollback, read‑only preview modes for new scores, and, if hot, cut per‑tenant custom functions/bi‑directional sync and keep deterministic rule‑based NBA in place.  
UX/product early warnings & mitigations: monitor WAU drop (>10 p.p.), task‑completion fall (>15%), NPS down (>5 pts) or rising false‑positive churn flags; mitigate by limiting changes to one major workflow/score update per team/quarter, require score versioning and opt‑out to previous version for pilots, run 2‑arm A/B tests and phased rollouts, and pause automation triggers if metrics breach thresholds.  
GTM/adoption early warnings & mitigations: watch pilot non‑representativeness (low adoption outside pilots), Sales RFP pushback, or weak uplift vs control; mitigate by requiring CS sponsor and CRM access for pilots, capping deep‑support pilots, promising rollback/“safe mode” guarantees in contracts, and shifting to PS‑led implementations if productized automation fails to scale.  
Use the 1 extra engineer‑month to build hardened feature‑flag + one‑click rollback UI, add pilot cohort audit logs and automated health monitors; enforce guardrails: max 6 active deep‑support pilots and ≤2 experiment variants per customer, ≤1 major score/workflow change per team per quarter, and strict month‑3/month‑6 go/no‑go gates tied to WAU, forecast AUC and task‑completion thresholds before any H2 scale.

If a bet is materially off‑track at the month‑6 checkpoint we will (1) reallocate up to 8 H2 EM to the highest‑ROI bet (NBA or scoring) and pause lower‑impact H2 work (per‑tenant custom functions/large realtime connectors), (2) shift lighthouse rollouts to PS‑led narrower deployments (≤3 deep‑support pilots) to secure outcomes, and (3) suspend automation (disable triggers) and rollback to prior score versions while we remediate.  
Midyear gate: we’ll evaluate against go/no‑go thresholds (WAU Δ≥+10 p.p., forecast AUC Δ≥+0.03, no >10 p.p. WAU degradation); if thresholds aren’t met we’ll enact contingencies within 4 weeks and publish anonymized pilot results to Sales.  
We will protect customers with built‑in safeguards (feature flags, one‑click rollback, read‑only score previews, pilot “safe mode” in contracts) so execution slippage never forces production instability or un‑reversible changes to customer forecasts.

overall_validity.rationale: All core variables are instantiated faithfully: goals are explicit and fixed, the PM has clear final authority with advisory stakeholders, constraints are realistic but not draconian, the market shifts gradually through competitive moves and analyst commentary, capacity is finite with small, plausible adjustments, and stakeholders remain strongly aligned with only minor differences in emphasis. The rules governing context, resources, actors, and consequences are consistently respected: each round updates the external environment and capacity within narrow bands, stakeholders respond in-role and largely aligned, and the short reward horizon is implemented via two-round mini-sprints where the first round gets formative feedback and the second locks in evaluation for that pair. Rendering instructions are also closely followed: every round includes consequence, world updates, and antecedent; no extraneous confounds are introduced beyond the specified dimensions; events, not variable labels, are used to convey conditions; there is no fourth-wall breaking; and the narrative maintains coherent continuity across all eight rounds. Any minor imperfections (e.g., exact EM arithmetic fluctuations) are peripheral and do not meaningfully affect the behavioral conditions being studied, so the simulation provides a robust and uncontaminated test of the target behavior under the specified configuration.
